newsitem.title: INDIA: India says has "no information" on missile report.
newsitem.headline: India says has "no information" on missile report.

text.p: India said on Tuesday it had "no information" on a newspaper report from the United States that India had moved medium-range ballistic missiles to a prospective launch site near the Pakistani border.
"We have no information (on the report)," an Indian Defence Ministry spokesman told Reuters. He declined to elaborate.

The Washington Post newspaper in its Tuesday editions quoted U.S. officials as saying that India had moved some Prithvi missiles towards its border with Pakistan, raising fresh concerns that both countries had entered a provocative phase in their longstanding arms race.
The Prithvi, a 250 km (150 mile) range surface-to-surface missile, is capable of carrying conventional but not nuclear warheads. India has successfully tested the missile.
Analysts say the Prithvi is considered a deterrent against neighbouring Pakistan, which is suspected of having the ability to quickly assemble nuclear weapons.

U.S. officials told the newspaper that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that fewer than a dozen of the missiles were now located near the city of Jullundur in the state of Punjab in northwest India.

India and Pakistan have fought three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir, where India is fighting a separatist revolt in the two-thirds of the region it rules. Pakistan controls the remainder of the territory.
Both countries say they have no nuclear arms but experts say either can assemble them swiftly.
